title: Data Analyst Interview Prep: SQL and Python with SQLite

goal.end_state.value: Write a join across orders, customers and products and explain why a row count changed; aggregate revenue by month and region with a HAVING filter; rank customers with a window function; find the first and the repeat purchase of each customer; load a SQLite table into pandas and clean it; compute a weekly retention cohort; explain a metric drop to a non-technical manager; answer a timed case question on the retailer's data.

goal.non_goals.value: No dashboards or BI tools, no machine learning, no database administration, no cloud warehouses, no statistics beyond means, medians and rates.

learner.who.value: Someone who has written basic Python and simple SELECT queries and is preparing for a junior or mid-level data analyst interview; they must reach the level of answering the role's SQL and Python rounds unaided.

learner.levels.value: One level; depth tags in the outline mark window functions and cohorts as the harder topics.

learner.time_budget.value: 20 to 30 hours, recomputed from the written pages before the first release.

sources.list.value: The SQLite documentation (public domain, paraphrased and cited); the Python standard library documentation (PSF licence, read only); the pandas documentation (BSD licence, read only). Every lesson is written in the course's own words.

sources.authority.value: The ranked skill list in interview.skills; every skill on it has at least one practice.

scope.depth.value: Core for joins, aggregation and pandas cleaning; deep for window functions, cohorts and the case questions; survey for query plans; prose only for explaining results to a manager. The tags live in the outline.

scope.ruled_out.value: No server databases, no notebooks, no cloud accounts, no network access at run time; SQLite and Python only.

scope.cut_candidates.value: Charting with a plotting library and A/B test statistics were both cut before numbering; neither is in the outline.

runtimes.languages.value: Python 3.13 with pandas 2.2, and SQLite 3.45 through Python's sqlite3 module, pinned in the runner image.

runtimes.coverage.value: Every SQL practice is SQL run through sqlite3, and every Python practice is Python; no practice is written twice. The two prose-only lessons in The interview section have no practice.

runtimes.offline.value: Everything: the retailer's database ships as a generated SQLite file inside the course.

runtimes.hardware.value: None; every practice runs on a laptop CPU in under a second.

practice.density.value: 2 to 3 code practices per lesson that runs code; the prose-only lessons have none. A quiz at the end of each section.

practice.shape.value: TODO functions beside the section they test, a starter that fails on an assertion, and at most 25 changed lines per practice.

practice.tryit.value: Yes: every practice has a try-it Run that prints the query result or the data frame before the learner edits.

practice.projects.value: One project per section on the retailer's data, with the first step shown in full and later steps as goals only.

quiz.placement.value: At the end of each section only; never inside a lesson or a project.

quiz.keys_in_page.value: Yes: the keys ship in the page source, and quizzes are for self-checking, not grading.

writing.reference.value: The pilot module's first lesson is the reference; each lesson stays under 900 words of prose.

writing.diagrams.value: Wherever a lesson explains how rows flow through a join, a grouping or a window: one diagram per such lesson.

writing.review_rule.value: The author reviews the pilot; after that the build runs without review unless the author asks for more.

narration.scope.value: Prose only, never code or quizzes.

narration.voice.reason: Chosen after the first release, when narration starts, from samples of the finished pilot lesson.

privacy.private_folder.value: .private/ at the repository root, ignored before anything is stored in it.

privacy.sample_data.value: A generated SQLite database for the fictional retailer Spokeline Cycles: invented customer names, no addresses, no emails, and a fixed random seed; scanned before every release.

publish.licence.value: MIT for the code and the text.

publish.preview.value: Locally, on port 8765, before any public site exists.

publish.pusher.value: The author only; Claude prepares the list and never pushes.

limits.agents.value: 4 agents, as a rolling queue where a slow one never blocks the rest.

limits.reporting.value: After each module, with the remaining estimate recomputed from written pages.

interview.skills.value: 1. SQL joins and aggregation [core]; 2. window functions [deep]; 3. data cleaning in pandas [core]; 4. retention and cohort metrics [deep]; 5. explaining results to non-technical colleagues [prose]; 6. reading a query plan [survey].

interview.format.value: A live SQL round, a take-home Python task and a case discussion; no system design, no algorithm puzzles.

interview.project.value: Spokeline Cycles, a fictional bicycle retailer whose orders database is used from the first module to the last.

Left joins and finding what is missing
From a query to a data frame
